div.head: Hl 10[a]
div.ab: Gif man oþerne tihte, siþþan he him byrigan gesealdne hæbbe, ⁊ ðonne ymb III niht gesecæn hiom sæmend (buton þam ufor leofre sio þe þa tihtlan age); siþþan sio sace gesemed sio, an seofan nihtum se man þam oþrum riht gedo, gecwime an feo oððe an aþe, swa hwæder swa him leofre sio.

Gif man oþerne tihte, siþþan he him byrigan gesealdne hæbbe, ðonne ymb III niht gesecæn hiom sæmend, buton þam ufor leofre sio þe þa tihtlan age. Siþþan sio sace gesemed sio; an seofan nihtum se man þam oþrum riht gedo, gecwime an feo oððe an aþe, swa hwæder swa him leofre sio.

Gif man oþerne tihte, siþþan he him byrigan gesealdne hæbbe, ⁊ ðonne ymb III niht, gesecæn hiom sæmend, buton þam ufor leofre sio þe þa tihtlan age. Siþþan sio sace gesemed sio, an seofan nihtum se man þam oþrum riht gedo, gecwime an feo oððe an aþe, swa hwæder swa him leofre sio.

Wenn jemand einen anderen bezichtigt, nachdem dieser ihm einen Bürgen bestellt hat, [so] sollen sie binnen 3 Nächten darauf sich einen Schiedsrichter aufsuchen (ausser wenn später[er Termin] demjenigen lieber ist, der die Klage erhebt); nachdem die Streitsache entschieden ist, erfülle der [beklagte] Mann in 7 Nächten dem anderen das Urtheil, passe es ihm in Werthzahlung oder durch [Reinigungs-]Eid, welches von beiden ihm [dem Beklagten] lieber sei.

If someone accuses another after the latter has provided him with a surety, [then] within 3 nights after that they are to seek themselves an arbitrator (unless a later [date] is preferred by the one who brings the charge); after the dispute is decided, let the [accused] man fulfil the judgment to the other within 7 nights, satisfying him by payment of value or by [exculpatory] oath, whichever of the two is preferred by him [the accused].

If one man charges another, after the other has provided him with a surety, then three days later they shall attempt to find an arbitrator, unless the accuser prefers a longer delay. Within a week after the suit has been decided by arbitration, the accused shall render justice to the other and satisfy him with money, or with an oath, whichever he [the accused] prefers.

If a man charges another, after he has given him surety, then three days later they are to seek for themselves an arbitrator, unless a later term be preferable to him who brings forward the charge. After the suit has been settled, the man is to do right to the other within seven days; he is to satisfy him with money or with oath, whichever he prefers. If then he will not do that, he shall then pay 100 shillings, without an oath, one day after the arbitration is over.

If a person brings a charge against another, after he has given him surety, and then within 3 nights, let them seek out for themselves an arbitrator, unless later be preferable to him who brings the charge; after the matter shall be arbitrated, in seven nights the person [charged] should do right to the other; let him satisfy [him] with property or with oath, whichever is preferable to him.

note.seg: to be deleted
H punctuates wrongly here
Vgl. Gl Streitgedinge 1; Schiedsgericht 3. — Über die 4 Anfangsworte s. o. 8¹
Cf. Gl Streitgedinge 1; Schiedsgericht 3. — On the 4 opening words see above 8¹
Wäre and im Texte richtig, und erst gedo das Nachsatzverb, so ergäbe sich eine für diesen Stil fast beispiellos lange Konstruktion; vgl. jedoch Ine 62
If and in the text were correct, and only gedo the verb of the main clause, the result would be a construction of almost unparalleled length for this style; cf., however, Ine 62

Schmid identifiziert ihn unrichtig mit den deman in c. 8. Die Wörter sema, semend, (ge)seman, som, gesom (auch mengl. some, semen) scheinen nirgends genau iudex, iudicare, iudicium zu entsprechen. — Es liegt vor die Spur einer Zeit ‘bevor es staatliche Gerichtsorganisation gab, als noch Vertrauensmänner von den Parteien zu Schiedsrichtern ernannt wurden oder mächtige Männer vermittelten und schlichteten’; W. Sickel Deutsche Freistaat 158

Schmid wrongly identifies him with the deman in c. 8. The words sema, semend, (ge)seman, som, gesom (also ME some, semen) seem nowhere to correspond exactly to iudex, iudicare, iudicium. — What we have here is the trace of a time ‘before there was any state organisation of courts, when men of trust were still appointed by the parties as arbitrators, or powerful men mediated and settled disputes’; W. Sickel Deutsche Freistaat 158
Verschoben auf weiter als 3 Tage
Postponed to more than 3 days
Nicht ‘Beklagtem’, s. Wb agan 2
Not ‘the defendant’; see Wb agan 2
Durch zweizüngig Urteil (s. d. Gl 6); vgl. Brunner II 363. 370
By a two-tongued judgment (see that word in Gl 6); cf. Brunner II 363. 370
Beklagter geniesst den Vorteil der Beweisnähe; s. d. Gl
The defendant enjoys the advantage of being nearer to the proof; see that word in Gl
Nicht ‘geschehe’ oder ‘befriedige ihn’; s. Wb gecweman
Not ‘let it be done’ or ‘satisfy him’; see Wb gecweman
Des vom Schiedsrichter Zuerkannten, d. i. eingeklagten Schadens vielleicht zuzüglich Busse, aber, da nicht vor ordentlichem, staatlichem Gericht, noch ohne Strafgeld
Of what was awarded by the arbitrator, i.e. of the damage claimed, perhaps plus compensation, but, since not before a regular state court, as yet without a fine
Nicht etwa ‘eidlichem Gelöbnis künftiger Urteilserfüllung’, wie Price und Gierke Schuld und Haft. 182 meinen
Not, say, ‘a sworn promise of future fulfilment of the judgment’, as Price and Gierke Schuld und Haft. 182 think
Über d in hwæðer o. 8²
On d in hwæðer above 8²
